subject: english
chapter_title: A Question of Trust: Horace Danby's Last Theft

concepts.title: Horace Danby: A Safebreaker with a Routine
concepts.definition: Horace Danby, a fifty-year-old locksmith by trade, is good and respectable to his neighbours, yet he robs one safe every year to buy rare books, hiding his secret passion behind an orderly life.
concepts.key_idea: He suffers bouts of sneezing, studies his targets for two weeks, and robs only enough to spend about fifteen thousand pounds a year on books through an agent.

solution_steps.explain: By day a lock maker with two helpers, by secret habit a thief who steals once a year.
He studies the house's rooms, wiring and paths for about a fortnight before acting.
The loot buys rare and expensive books through an agent, feeding his love of reading.

concepts.title: The Robbery at Shotover Grange
concepts.definition: Horace enters Shotover Grange while the family is away, intending to rob the safe holding jewels worth fifteen thousand pounds, but his sneezing fits and the arrival of a woman posing as the owner's wife unsettle his plan.
concepts.key_idea: Hiding behind a flower vase, he watches the safe's jewels and only needs the correct combination to finish the job quietly.

solution_steps.explain: Shotover Grange stood on a hill, its owners away, and the safe in the drawing room held jewels.

solution_steps.action: note the flaw in his health
solution_steps.explain: Flowers in the room set off Hay fever sneezes that threatened his silence.
A young woman in the doorway claims to be the mistress of the house, turning the thief into the prey.

concepts.title: The Clever Stranger and the Safe Opened
concepts.definition: The woman blackmails Horace with the threat of prison, asking him to open the safe because she has forgotten the numbers, and he, trusting her story, opens it and hands over the jewels before slipping away.
concepts.key_idea: Horace cuts his finger on the knife she offers, breaks into the safe using his skill with locks, and walks free only to be arrested days later.

solution_steps.explain: She pretends to be the wife who needs the jewels for a party and threatens to call the police.
Horace remembers a magazine article about the combination and opens the safe with trembling care.
His fingerprint on the knife betrayed him, since the real mistress had never met the thief's tale before.

concepts.title: Honour among Thieves: The Story's Irony
concepts.definition: The story asks whether there is honour among thieves, and answers with irony: Horace, the professional thief, is himself robbed by a smoother criminal, and his refusal to confess costs him his freedom.
concepts.key_idea: Shocked by being tricked, Horace now plans to rob only safes of safe-owners, and in prison he rages at the idea of anyone doubting the honesty of locks.

solution_steps.explain: Horace robs safes with tools; the woman robs Horace with a lie, trusting his fear.
Horace trusts her story, she betrays him, and his fingerprints complete his downfall.
The man who never trusted anyone is undone by his single act of trusting.
